name: Scripted sessions that end right and requirements met
purpose: A scripted session answers every turn and ends cleanly, and a person working with the AI while it works can watch, stop, resume, steer, see helpers, approve and read the result on two harnesses.
record: One number: the share of scripted-stdin sessions that come out right (every turn reaches the front door in order, nothing a person typed is lost, a question is answered by the next line, the wanted text is shown, the session ends cleanly), balanced with time by [balance.terminal_session]; weights and budgets fixed in esoi.toml before any arm was scored. Kinds of case, as case sources of one component: turn, command, ask, exit (evaluation/terminal_session/build_cases.py). First stage, model-free: a stub front door answers each line from the case, so the check costs nothing. Later stages (a real offline run of the whole hub, a person's trial) rise in fidelity and keep this number. Added case kind attend (evaluation/terminal_session/sessions.py): scripted sessions on the hub's own loop (a scripted completion behind the loop runner) and on a fake that keeps the stream runner's contract, each scored by named checks against requirement ids X1 to X23 of docs/explanation/working-with-the-ai-while-it-works.md; the share of cases right is the number, and per-requirement shares are reported.
disadvantages: Few invented sessions against a stub front door: it shows the loop holds, not that a person finds the screen clear. A real run of the hub and a person's trial are not in this stage. Scripted harnesses prove the contract, not that a real model's run feels right; a person's trial on a real terminal is the later stage.
cascading_conditionals: free [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the arm was recorded on the same cases]
